title: Basic Biosafety Level (BSL) Concepts

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: An introduction to the tiered system of laboratory practices, safety equipment, and facility design features used to match containment to the risk of the work being performed.
explanation: BSLs (commonly described from BSL-1, the least stringent, to BSL-4, the most stringent) combine standard microbiological practices, special practices, safety equipment (primary barriers, e.g. BSCs), and facility design (secondary barriers) appropriate to a specific activity's risk assessment. As covered in the 'BSL vs. Risk Group' concept entry, the correct BSL for a task is determined by a risk assessment, not read directly off a fixed organism-to-BSL lookup table.
keyPractices: Follow the standard microbiological practices required at every BSL (e.g. handwashing, no eating/drinking in the lab, waste decontamination).
Understand what special practices and equipment apply above the baseline level for the specific work being done.
Do not assume containment requirements transfer unchanged between different procedures using the same organism.
scopeCaveat: This entry introduces the general concept only — the current, complete requirements for a specific BSL and organism should always be confirmed against the current edition of the BMBL and the relevant institutional biosafety committee guidance, not assumed from memory.
